comparisons.peer_topic: High Quality Liquid Assets and Liquidity Coverage Ratio
comparisons.peer_summary: Global Liquidity Sources are substantially the same in composition as High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) under U.S. Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) rules, though HQLA is calculated at a lower value incorporating regulatory deductions. The company's average consolidated HQLA was $623 billion and $590 billion for the three months ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, resulting in average consolidated LCRs of 113 percent and 115 percent respectively, with fluctuations attributed to normal business flows.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose their High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) and unencumbered securities as core components of their total liquidity sources. JPMorgan reports specific end-of-period balances for 2024, stating it held approximately $834 billion in HQLA and $594 billion in unencumbered marketable securities, totaling approximately $1.4 trillion in liquidity sources. In contrast, Bank of America reports its average consolidated HQLA on a net basis as $623 billion for the three months ended December 31, 2024, rather than a static end-of-period total for the full year, and explicitly notes that its Global Liquidity Sources (GLS) are substantially the same in composition as HQLA but valued differently due to regulatory deductions.

sentences.text: • As of December 31, 2024, the Firm had eligible end-of-period High Quality Liquid Assets ("HQLA") of approximately $834 billion and unencumbered marketable securities with a fair value of approximately $594 billion, resulting in approximately $1.4 trillion of liquidity sources. Refer to Liquidity Risk Management on pages 108-115 for additional information.
Our GLS are substantially the same in composition to what qualifies as High Quality Liquid Assets (HQLA) under the final U.S. Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) rules.
Our average consolidated HQLA, on a net basis, was $623 billion and $590 billion for the three months ended December 31, 2024 and 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, Citigroup had approximately $933 billion of available liquidity resources, consisting of $554 billion in end-of-period HQLA, $227 billion in additional unencumbered HQLA, and $152 billion in unused borrowing capacity from FHLB and Federal Reserve Bank discount windows.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup disclose specific dollar amounts of HQLA and unencumbered assets as part of their total available liquidity resources as of December 31, 2024. JPMorgan reports approximately $834 billion in HQLA and $594 billion in unencumbered marketable securities, resulting in approximately $1.4 trillion of total liquidity sources. Citigroup reports $554 billion in end-of-period HQLA and $227 billion in additional unencumbered HQLA (plus $152 billion in unused borrowing capacity), resulting in approximately $933 billion of available liquidity resources. While both metrics include HQLA and unencumbered securities, JPMorgan’s metric is labeled 'liquidity sources' while Citigroup’s is 'available liquidity resources' including borrowing capacity.

sentences.text: • As of December 31, 2024, the Firm had eligible end-of-period High Quality Liquid Assets ("HQLA") of approximately $834 billion and unencumbered marketable securities with a fair value of approximately $594 billion, resulting in approximately $1.4 trillion of liquidity sources. Refer to Liquidity Risk Management on pages 108-115 for additional information.

As of December 31, 2024, Citigroup had approximately $933 billion of available liquidity resources to support client and business needs, including end-of-period HQLA ($554 billion); additional unencumbered HQLA, including excess liquidity held at bank entities that is non-transferable to other entities within Citigroup ($227 billion); and unused borrowing capacity from available assets not already accounted for within Citi's HQLA to support additional advances from the Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) and the Federal Reserve Bank discount window ($152 billion).

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidate gs_2024_7_D258 describes the regulatory minimum LCR requirement (100%) and rule definition, not the specific volume of HQLA or total liquidity sources held. The candidate gs_2024_7_D257 discusses 'other unencumbered assets' explicitly excluded from the GCLA (Goldman's equivalent of HQLA/LCR buffers), making it a contrasting definition rather than a comparable liquidity source metric. No candidate provides a comparable aggregate HQLA or total liquidity source figure.

The retrieved candidates ms_2024_7_D134 and ms_2024_7_D137 define the composition of HQLA held in subsidiaries and the purpose of the LCR rule, respectively. They do not disclose the total amount of HQLA or total liquidity resources held by Morgan Stanley as of year-end 2024, which is required to compare with JPMorgan's reported $1.4 trillion liquidity sources.
